entry.title: Content pipeline: emit delta word indexes and fold them at load (#424)
entry.content:
Content pipeline: emit delta word indexes and fold them at load (#424)

A module's index file was cumulative through itself, so a course's index set
grew quadratically with its ladder. hi-mr reached thirty modules earlier today
and the curve became measurable rather than projected: 1.2 MB raw of index for
one course, every byte of it warmed for offline, against ~115 KB if each file
carried only its own additions.

Each file now carries the surfaces its module is the FIRST to teach, marked
`delta: true`, beside the ladder it sits in and the folded totals.
`loadIndex` fetches that ladder's deltas and folds them earliest-first, which
is what preserves first-occurrence-wins, and checks its own work: a fold whose
size disagrees with the file's `surfaceCount` throws instead of resolving half
a ladder. Everything above content.ts — the resolver, the why panel, the
tests — still sees the cumulative shape, and always has.

The change rests on one claim, so that is what is tested: fold(deltas) equals
the cumulative index key for key and entry for entry, for every module of
every course (tools/delta-index.test.ts). The reader's fold is written out by
hand there rather than imported, the way a round-trip test writes the inverse.

Measured: hi-mr's index set 1.2 MB → 79 KB raw, `course:hi-mr` 542.0 → 468.5
KiB gzip, `precache:hi-mr` 758.4 → 685.1; the other eight sit at 20-31 KB raw.
Gzip moves 14% because cumulative files compress well — it is the raw bytes
and the growth curve that move by an order of magnitude, and the curve is what
mattered at fifty modules.

Proved in a real build, not only in tests: L3-M10's sentence detail resolves
its why rows after folding thirty deltas, each index URL is fetched once, and
a warmed course boots and resolves with the network off.

BUILD | BUDGET.

entry.content:
Content: ratify the L4 and L5 lists, and give two deferrals an address (#423)

The twenty jobs #417 added as `draft: true` are ratified as drafted, the way
#112 ratified L2/L3 — but reviewed against authored content rather than
against the plan alone: hi-mr's L2 and L3 shipped the same day, so these
twenty were read next to twenty that have actually been written. Every
levels.json now says `Ratified list (#423)` on L4 and L5; the `draft` flag
stays until each level is authored, as L2/L3's did.

Two amendments came out of that review.

L3-M10's job said "written unaided", which described the notebook exit
#348/#349 retired — the exit ritual is generate-and-comprehend and nothing in
it is written. All nine levels.json now read "built from the whole ladder",
and hi-mr's shipped L3-M10 moved with it: the module's own `job`, its brief,
and the rule that quotes the phrase. The new phrase is also true of it — that
module added one surface.

And the passive now has an owner. docs/50 §3 deferred it out of L3 without
saying where it goes, which is how a deferral becomes an orphan; it lands at
L4-M7 (official talk — announcements and counters are where a learner meets
it) with L4-M2 as its second home.

Two things the review deliberately left alone, both recorded in docs/48 §4 so
the next reader does not re-open them: L4-M10's six sentences against L3/L5's
eight (the cap is a ceiling and that item carries dialogue), and L4-M7's
overlap with L2-M1 and L3-M8 (L2 teaches which register to speak, L3 puts you
at the counter, L4 is the register you hear there and do not speak back).

entry.title: Content pipeline: report and ratchet shown-but-untaught surfaces (#491)
entry.content:
Content pipeline: report and ratchet shown-but-untaught surfaces (#491)

`checkComprehensionPool` has always failed a build when a pool token did not
resolve. Nothing checked what a module SHOWS outside the pool, so a
`variations[].display` could carry a word no row owns — the gap #282 closed by
hand for seven hi-mr lines, which has reopened in every course since.

`checkShownSurfaces` walks every sentence display and every variation display
against the module's own cumulative index. It REPORTS rather than fails, and
that is the design, not a compromise: across the nine shipped courses it finds
133 distinct surfaces, and they are three different things. A proper noun
rides unindexed by #61 and no row should ever own it. A forward reference is a
word the ladder teaches two rungs later — untaught for the learner standing
here, so a real defect whose fix is a rewritten variation. The rest are simply
never taught, and mostly want a `forms` entry on the row that should own them.
Failing the build on all three would reject correct content and would spring a
nine-language sweep on whoever ran the next build.

So the line is held by a ratchet instead. `npm run content:build` prints one
line per course; `tools/shown-surfaces.test.ts` pins a per-course baseline that
may fall and may not rise, and a course with no baseline entry must have none.
That is what makes it bite for the 320 L2/L3 modules still to author, which is
where it saves the most.

docs/52-shown-surface-findings.md is the standing list, classified per course,
with what a sweep would have to decide. Two things it makes visible: hi-en (the
course whose L2 is English) carries 30 of the 133, and the twenty hi-mr L2/L3
modules added earlier today contribute none — they were audited by hand against
this exact rule, which is the manual work this check replaces.

entry.title: Authoring: ship `verified: true` in the authoring change, by default
entry.content:
Authoring: ship `verified: true` in the authoring change, by default

The two-step — author `verified: false`, flip it in a second pass — recorded
nothing the signature does not, and left correct content out of a learner
build for no gain. From now on a module is authored with `verifiedBy` and
`verifiedAt` already on it, and the wave's review-doc section lands in the
same commit.

Three places carry it so no future session re-derives it: the prompt's
round-trip block (step 4 said "never set it yourself" and now says what to
set and what to write beside it), the README's gate paragraph, and a new
CLAUDE.md that also states the seam rules a level is expected to hold — no
level edits a file below it, a shown surface is a taught surface, paradigms
have one home.

What does NOT change: `tools/validate.ts` still rejects a verified module
with no signature, so the signature is the record; and the native-speaker
gate is still a separate, stricter bar that is unmet. Every review doc ends
in numbered open questions for it, and an authoring wave may not close one by
rewriting a shipped module.

entry.title: Content hi-mr: author and verify L3-M6…M10 — the level closes (#479)
entry.content:
Content hi-mr: author and verify L3-M6…M10 — the level closes (#479)

M6 adds nouns and no grammar: feelings ride frames owned since L1-M9, and the
delta is which verb each takes — काळजी/भीती on वाटणे, आनंद/दुःख on होणे, राग
on येणे, a split Hindi cannot predict. वाटणे is not re-opened; the row stays
L3-M3's. Two gender flips against Hindi in one module. +17.

M7 is one frame told plainly: the body part is the subject and there is no
दर्द noun at all, so both Hindi routes are closed. Agreement with the part
makes डोकं, हात and डोळे grammar rather than vocabulary. -कडे stands bare for
the first time, pointing back at डावीकडे. +20.

M8 turns on भरणे — a stomach, a bill, a form, exactly as भरना does — with the
past agreeing with the thing filled. सही is the false friend (Hindi's
"correct" lives in बरोबर), and महत्त्वाचं is a genitive in disguise, so it
needs no new rule. +24.

M9 is आहे against असते, with Hindi's है/होता है as the free half, and L2-M7's
continuous describing a street instead of a phone call. Festival names take
rows like any other common noun, and the module describes what a visitor
would see without asserting any practice as universal — written into the
rules, not only the sentences. +33.

M10 is the exit, and its number is the proof: +1 surface for the whole module.
Every row is a re-show whose note explains the word's job in a story; the
accounts run four to seven sentences under an eight-sentence ceiling, each
with a reason and a feeling, and the last tells the same day to a friend and
to an elder.

The level closes: 100 sentences, 120 pool items, 441 → 633 surfaces, `draft`
dropped on L3, and the strict build ships hi-mr 30 modules. No L1 or L2 file
changed in the whole level; every cell L2 left open was opened as a new row.
`src/course/types.test.ts` pins 110 module files; the README carries the
level's paragraph.

Reviewed in docs/51-llm-review-hi-mr-L3.md, wave 3 — open questions 87-96.

entry.title: Content hi-mr: author and verify L3-M3, L3-M4, L3-M5 (#470)
entry.content:
Content hi-mr: author and verify L3-M3, L3-M4, L3-M5 (#470)

M3 "Opinions with reasons" opens वाटणे — the row decision 4 of the briefs
assigned here, with its note written true of both jobs so M6 can point back
rather than open a second family. की does the second of its three jobs, the
agreement words (बरोबर, चूक, खरं) need no grammar at all, and softening stays
in words: कदाचित in front, ना at the end. आहे's own past — होता/होती/होतं —
arrives on the last sentence, because a reason often lies in the past. +26.

M4 "If and then" takes the conditional in the order a speaker meets it: जर …
तर with तर named as the half that never drops, advice on -आयला पाहिजे,
पाहिजे's second job beside L1-M3's हवं, and exactly ONE counterfactual frame
with the note saying in words that the system is L4-M3's. नाहीतर closes it as
two owned words in one shape. +22.

M5 "What someone said" is the cheapest lesson in the level and says so:
Marathi does not backshift and neither does Hindi. The work is म्हणणे, whose
past agrees with the speaker and never takes ने, set directly against L2-M10's
त्याने सांगितलं, which takes both — that pair is the module. असं lets the
report follow the words; विचारणे's reported question keeps its question word
where the answer would sit. +8.

बोललो stays pinned: M5 does not stretch म्हणणे over बोलणे to close docs/15
Q29, per the level's decision 3. No L1 or L2 file changed.

entry.title: Content hi-mr: author and verify L3-M1, L3-M2 (#461)
entry.content:
Content hi-mr: author and verify L3-M1, L3-M2 (#461)

The first two rungs of the first L3 in any course, authored from the #452
briefs against the real 441-surface index.

M1 "Your day, in detail" is the -ऊन converb and almost nothing else: a day
told at length has no full stops in it, and Hindi's करके makes the move free,
so the ending is the whole delta. The rule that earns the module is that the
converb carries no person and no gender — S01 and S07 are the same chain under
मी and ती, and only the final verb moves. Not joining the steps with आणि is
tagged interference, because that is exactly what the Hindi habit produces.
Two items run to two sentences, the first in the course. +12 surfaces.

M2 "Work and study" opens the genitive as a system — what L2-M2 taught in one
frame and deliberately stopped at. All five cells land on real nouns
(ऑफिसचं काम, कंपनीची नोकरी, भावाचे मित्र, ऑफिसच्या खोल्या), the law itself
transfers from का/की/के, and the delta is the fusion plus the owner's bend.
-मध्ये arrives beside L1-M7's -त, split by borrowed against native noun, and
अभ्यास carries the false friend: Hindi's "practice", Marathi's schoolwork, and
masculine where Hindi's पढ़ाई is feminine. +28 surfaces.

Two cells L2 had left open are opened here rather than by editing an L2 file:
जेवतो/जेवते (L2 taught only the past and the right-now) and the -चा/-चे/-च्या
genitive cells. No L1 or L2 file changed.

entry.title: Briefs: write the ten hi-mr L3 briefs (#452)
entry.content:
Briefs: write the ten hi-mr L3 briefs (#452)

The first L3 briefed anywhere, and the first level in this repo planned
against a verified level that is itself above L1. Pinned against the real
cumulative index through L2-M10 — rebuilt and read, 441 surfaces, maxSpan 1 —
not L1's 222 and not a remembered figure.

The four decisions, in the header and repeated in every module's notes, with
the full record in docs/50-hi-mr-L3-brief-decisions.md: fields unchanged from
L1 and L2; register carried from L2 with #422's chip; what L2 withheld now
owned — the genitive as a system at M2, the -ऊन converb at M1, conditionals
at M4 (one counterfactual frame, the system is L4-M3's), reported speech at
M5 on the की L2-M9 left unfenced; and the passive kept out of L3 entirely.

Two debts stay standing rather than being quietly closed: L1-M9's बोललो
remains the pinned index miss (M5's note says why merging बोलणे into म्हणणे
would poison both rows), and docs/49's open questions 49-70 are native-pass
items, not authoring ones.

Seams assigned up front so no two modules can claim one lexeme: वाटणे has two
jobs and one row (M3's, with M6 pointing back), भरणे stays L2-M8's, की stays
L2-M9's across all three jobs, -कडे stands bare for the first time at M7.

Bounds climb 10 → 11 → 12, pools 12, M10's items capped at eight sentences
with a new-word spend that should be zero. `tools/course-briefs.test.ts` pins
the module list, the bounds ladder, the two governing decisions, the seam
owners and the two standing debts.

No content authored. `npm run content:prompt -- hi-mr L3-M1` renders from the
real L2-M10 index.

entry.title: Content hi-mr: author and verify L2-M6…M10 — the level closes (#443)
entry.content:
Content hi-mr: author and verify L2-M6…M10 — the level closes (#443)

M6 assembles the suggestion frame out of pieces already owned (-ऊ + या),
splits ask from propose where Hindi folds both into चलें, and lands the clock
hours — docs/15 Q28's second instalment. येशील finally reaches a display,
which docs/15 Q25 left open. +11 surfaces.

M7 spends the module on one tense: बोलतोय · बोलतेय · बोलतंय, with the
unknown-caller neuter as the interference and the written बोलत आहे shown
beside the spoken form so both resolve. The plain present's about-to job is a
new use of a shape owned since L1-M4. बोलणे's rows open — docs/15 Q29. +15.

M8 is the survival module: सापडणे against मिळणे (M5's mirror seam), the -त
नाही frame where nothing agrees, हरवला/संपले on L1-M5's law against विसरलो
which agrees with the person, and जरा मदत करा · हळू बोला · पुन्हा सांगा. +27.

M9 glues -पेक्षा over the oblique bend, keeps जास्त/कमी invariable, makes
सगळ्यात parseable on sight, and splits की from किंवा by sentence type. +16.

M10 brings the oldest debt due: the ने L1-M5 fenced off (docs/08 Q20) arrives
as त्याने · तिने · त्यांनी with object agreement unchanged — S03 and S07 hold
the subject still while the verb moves. भेटणे takes -ला on the person met and
agrees with the meeter; सांगितलं is flagged irregular. Accounts on आधी · मग ·
शेवटी, past tense only. +22.

Two brief claims the rebuilt index corrected, both recorded in docs/49: झालं
and आलो were never taught in L1, so they open here as their own rows. No L1
file changed in the whole level.

The level closes: 100 sentences, 120 pool items, 222 → 441 surfaces, `draft`
dropped on L2 in levels.json, and the strict build ships hi-mr 20 modules.
`src/course/types.test.ts` now pins 100 module files, and the README carries
the level's paragraph.

Reviewed in docs/49-llm-review-hi-mr-L2.md, wave 3 — open questions 62-70.

entry.title: Content hi-mr: author and verify L2-M3, L2-M4, L2-M5 (#434)
entry.content:
Content hi-mr: author and verify L2-M3, L2-M4, L2-M5 (#434)

L2-M3 "Describing things" walks the whole agreement grid: -ा · -ी · -ं
singular, -े · -्या · -ी plural, with the two loud cells shown as pairs — the
feminine plural Hindi never bends (मोठी पिशवी / मोठ्या पिशव्या) and the neuter
plural spelled exactly like the feminine singular (मोठी खोली / मोठी घरं). Noun
plurals ride the same seam, each pointing back to its L1 first-teach. +38.

L2-M4 "Getting around" is two glued endings: -ला on the destination over
L1-M7's oblique bend, starred against Hindi's bare noun, and -ने on the
vehicle, with the note kept narrow because -ने's past-tense job is M10's. The
बस key stays the vehicle's, as M1's बसा row promised. +28.

L2-M5 "Food and hosting" ships the host's script (घ्या, आणखी, तुम्हाला) and
the refusal ladder (नको → आता नको → पुरे → पोट भरलं), warns that a Hindi
speaker's "बस!" at a Marathi table is the vehicle, and keeps मिळणे to its half
of मिलना so सापडणे's seam survives for M8. तीन · चार · पाच pay docs/15 Q28.
+22.

All three carry the full five enrichment blocks, not only M3 which the law
compels: every hi-mr module has since L1-M1, and a learner should not feel the
ladder thin out mid-level. Every display in every sentence, variation and pool
item resolves against its own cumulative index — the #282 discipline, checked
mechanically; proper nouns ride unindexed by #61.

entry.title: Content hi-mr: author and verify L2-M1, L2-M2 (#425)
entry.content:
Content hi-mr: author and verify L2-M1, L2-M2 (#425)

The first content above L1 in any course. It proves the chain on a second
level: the prompt CLI crossed the level boundary (L2-M1 was generated against
L1-M10's real index, L2-M2 against L2-M1's), the M1-M3 enrichment law read the
module number rather than the level, and `prerequisites` stayed inside the
level — L2-M1 lists [], and the seal rule carries the cross-level dependency.

L2-M1 "Asking politely" is the register module: the imperative pair (bare stem
for तू — दे · कर · ये; stem + -आ for तुम्ही — द्या · करा · या · बसा), the
starred -इए tier Marathi does not have, and आप ≠ आपण spent as a rule and a
mistake. #422's chip carries the tier the briefs had to smuggle into `usage`:
five formal, four informal, one neutral. +12 surfaces.

L2-M2 "Describing people" pays L1's pronoun debt (docs/19 Q40): तो · ती · ते
as one row-set true of both its jobs, आहेत as the fourth cell of आहे, the
वडील/आई respect asymmetry told honestly, the adjective split that previews M3,
neuter मूल, and the genitive in one frame — माझ्या भावाचं नाव. +28 surfaces.

Seams held per docs/26 §4: द्या stays L1-M8's row, बसा's row lists no bare बस,
या's note is true of the invite particle too, मदत is left for M8, and no L1
file changed. The briefs' stale index figure (215) is corrected to the rebuilt
222 in both `tools/course-briefs.ts` and docs/26.

standing authority, ending in open questions 49-54 for a native pass.

entry.title: Schema: add `formal` to the sentence register enum (#422)
entry.content:
Schema: add `formal` to the sentence register enum (#422)

Every course's L2-M1 is "Asking politely", and four of the nine L2s teach a
polite address that is a verb paradigm rather than a word. The chip had two
values, so hi-mr's L2 briefs and en-it's L1 header both recorded the same
workaround: carry the tier in the `usage` line, in words. It now lives as data.

The enum is spelled in four places and all four move together — the schema
(the only enforced one), `Register`, `ModuleSentence`, and the chip's comment
in `SentenceScreen.module.css`. `UsageSection` prints the raw value, so no
strings key and no course bundle changes.

`tools/register.test.ts` pins both ends against the real validator: `formal`
validates, `polite` and a stray-cased `Formal` do not — widening it once did
not turn it into free text.

hi-mr's L2-M1 brief now chips the formal end instead of smuggling it into
`usage`; docs/26 §2 carries the addendum; the en-it, en-fr and en-de L1
headers say the enum HAD two values when they were authored, so the record
stays true without reopening those courses.

entry.title: SentenceScreen: split SentenceDetail into ten section components
entry.content:
SentenceScreen: split SentenceDetail into ten section components

SentenceDetail was 482 lines (322 code), the largest function in src/,
with ten data-section blocks nested up to ~13 levels deep at the same
altitude as route derivation. Each block is now its own component under
src/screens/sentence/ — HeroSection, WordsSection, TrapSection,
GlossSection, RulesSection, SoundSection, VariationsSection,
MistakeSection, UsageSection, MnemonicSection — taking { sentence } plus
l2, strings or the module's rules where the section needs them. A
section with nothing to show returns null, so the "renders NOTHING" rule
moved with the markup. WordRow and VariationRow keep each list body at
two levels; changedTokens went with its only caller.

Beside them: Deeper owns the disclosure's state and button and takes the
six deeper sections as children, so the frozen order stays in one place;
SentencePager owns the nav and its own navigate(replace); and
useLadderHandOver owns the hand-over / hand-back derivation, with
isOpenableRung replacing the same three-clause predicate written three
times. SentenceDetail is 78 lines: guards, the hand-over hook, and the
composition in the same order as before.

Proof, per docs/code-readability-conventions.md: headless Chromium
against the local build renders /sentence/L1-M1-S01 (hi-mr; every

entry.title: content-build: split buildContent into read, emit and report phases
entry.content:
content-build: split buildContent into read, emit and report phases

buildContent was 201 code lines nesting four deep (for row → for file →
if (!result.ok) → for issue) with nine continue statements, and its body
already labelled the three phases with banner comments. It is now twelve
lines that read as the pipeline: readCoursePlans, then either the FAIL
block or emitTree followed by reportLines.

Read phase: readCoursePlans walks the manifest and asks readCoursePlan for
each row, which returns CoursePlan | null instead of continuing. The
per-file body became readValidModule, returning ValidModule | null — a
ShippedModule plus the romanization warning it would earn, so gateCourse
can decide what ships, what is held back and which warnings print without
re-reading anything. checkComprehensionPools carries the #416 by-id lookup
unchanged. Emit phase: emitTree replaces outRoot and returns the
courseId → ids map; emitCourse writes one folder; emittedManifest builds
courses.json. Report phase: reportLines, courseLines, nothingShippedLine,
summaryLine. GatedModule names the { id, reason } shape describeGated and
summariseReasons already took. No function in the new code nests past two.

Proof, per docs/code-readability-conventions.md: strict `npm run
content:build` twice on main gave byte-identical trees (208 files) and
identical reports; a corrupted index file in a copy made `diff -r` report
it; strict and --with-unverified --with-fixtures trees and reports built
after this change diff empty against their baselines. The FAIL path, which
the tree diff cannot see, was run on both versions against a copy of
content/ with an orphan course folder, a missing strings key, an invalid
module JSON and a module dropped from levels.json: 83 identical lines,
exit 1, same order.

Closes #413

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: content-build: pair word indexes by module id, not array position
entry.content:
content-build: pair word indexes by module id, not array position

buildWordIndex returned a positional array and buildContent re-paired
shipped[i] with indexes[i] by shared counter, with an `undefined` guard
that would have skipped the comprehension-pool check silently had the two
ever drifted. It now returns a Map<moduleId, WordIndexFile> (insertion
order is still ladder order, so the emit and report loops iterate
.values() in the same sequence as before), and the caller looks each
module's index up by id; a miss throws, because buildWordIndex builds one
per module it is given and a missing one is a bug, not a module to skip.

The body nested five deep with two continues at the innermost level. It is
now one loop over the shipped modules; indexModule, indexWord and
indexSurface each sit at one altitude and nest at most two, and the
empty-surface skip is a filter rather than a continue (surfaceIndexKeys('')
would hand back the empty key). maxSpan is computed from the map at write
time by maxSpanOf instead of carried as a running maximum — the same
value, since keys are never removed.

Proof, per docs/code-readability-conventions.md: strict `npm run
content:build` twice on main gave byte-identical trees (208 files, 90
index files) and identical reports; a deliberately corrupted index file in
a copy made `diff -r` report it; the tree and report built after this
change diff empty against the baseline.

Closes #416
